nodes.label: Codebase Review (Efficiency, API Contract, Maintainability, Scalability)
nodes.rationale: Written as an executable work list for an implementing agent rather than prose: each finding states problem, why it matters, exact fix, and acceptance criteria, with a prescribed implementation order (quick wins → contract/compliance → efficiency → docs last, so docs describe the post-fix state).

nodes.label: Standing Rules for the Implementer
nodes.rationale: Never weaken safety behavior (blocked path, force_append_disclaimer, bilingual coverage, prompt safety rules must stay at least as strict; when in doubt fail closed); preserve the services/routes/schemas layering; keep the app_state module-global patching pattern working; run pytest after each finding.

nodes.label: F1: Chat History Injected Twice into Every Prompt
nodes.rationale: MessagesPlaceholder('chat_history') and a {chat_history} slot in the human template both render the same message list, so every turn pays double token cost and the model additionally sees raw HumanMessage(content=...) repr text, degrading quality.

nodes.label: F2: Blocking Sync Work on the Event Loop
nodes.rationale: Two paths: async upload_image calls classify_skin_image synchronously (PIL + TensorFlow predict freeze all concurrent SSE streams, and the lazy lru_cache model load makes the first upload absorb multi-second latency), and the Chroma retriever's blocking embed+query saturates LangChain's bounded sync thread pool. Fix is asyncio.to_thread for classification plus an end-to-end async retrieval path, keeping sync paths for the ingestion CLI.

nodes.label: F3: SessionMemory Grows Unbounded and Reads Without Its Lock
nodes.rationale: Turns are bounded per session but sessions are never evicted, and each upload mints a fresh UUID, so memory leaks linearly with unique sessions. add_turn locks but get_history does not — a latent race once eviction mutates the dict. Fix adds TTL + LRU eviction with time.monotonic and makes get_history async and lock-guarded.

nodes.label: F4: SSE Error Path Leaks Internals, Never Logs, Never Emits done
nodes.rationale: Four defects in one except block: str(e) is sent to the browser (information disclosure), nothing is logged server-side (undiagnosable failures), no terminal done frame (clients hang), and CancelledError on disconnect isn't an Exception so add_turn/log_query are silently skipped. The done frame must move to finally, but guarded so GeneratorExit on disconnect doesn't raise 'async generator ignored GeneratorExit'.

nodes.label: F5: Client detection Field Is a Prompt-Injection Channel
nodes.rationale: Unconstrained client strings are model_dump_json'd into the SYSTEM prompt slot, so a crafted label can carry 'SYSTEM OVERRIDE' text into the highest-privilege position and undermine prompt rule 7. Fix constrains label to a Literal and model_version to a pattern, and renders detection explicitly instead of dumping JSON. The schema must duplicate the label values rather than import from services/ — layering rule — with a test asserting the two lists match.

nodes.label: F6: Evidence Filter Fails Open When a Chunk Has No Score
nodes.rationale: metadata.get('score', 1.0) means a scoreless doc passes the gate. Latent today because the adapter always sets score, but a gate protecting medical answers should fail closed by construction, not by luck of the current backend. One-character fix: default 0.0.

nodes.label: F7: Blocked Responses Skip Disclaimer, Logging, and Memory
nodes.rationale: Safety-blocked turns violate the stated 'disclaimer on every turn' guarantee, are invisible to compliance review because no log_query entry is written, and leave the model without context that it refused. Fix force-appends the disclaimer, logs with a new classification parameter passed from BOTH branches, and records the turn.

nodes.label: F8: SSE Chunk Schema Untyped; CitationOut Dead
nodes.rationale: The SSE event stream IS the public API contract of /api/chat, yet type is a bare str (typos ship silently) and citations are list[dict] despite a correctly-shaped CitationOut model sitting unused three lines below.

nodes.label: F9: Citation Events Report Every Retrieved Chunk
nodes.rationale: Emitting on retriever completion means the UI shows sources the answer never used, extract_citations() is dead in the app path, and citations_used is hardcoded empty so the offline quality metric is permanently zero. Citations are only knowable after the token stream ends, so emission must move there.

nodes.label: F10: Token Usage Logged as 0/0
nodes.rationale: ChatOpenAI(stream_usage=True) attaches usage_metadata to the final streamed chunk; that chunk has empty content so the existing `if token:` guard already skips emitting it. Without this, cost for an OpenAI-backed medical service is unmeasurable.

nodes.label: F11: Upload Buffers Unlimited Bytes and Leaks Paths
nodes.rationale: await file.read() buffers the entire body before the 10MB check, so a multi-GB upload is held in memory then rejected — a memory-exhaustion DoS. Also trusts client content_type, and the 503 detail interpolates FileNotFoundError which contains the server's model filesystem path.

nodes.label: F12: session_id Is an Unvalidated Free-Form String
nodes.rationale: Sessions are minted server-side as UUID4 but /api/chat accepts any string, so histories can be read or poisoned by guessing and arbitrarily long ids become unbounded dict keys — which compounds F3. Format validation is explicitly a partial fix; true authorization is out of scope.

nodes.label: F13: get_settings() Re-Parses .env on Every Call
nodes.rationale: Per-request filesystem read and parse, and worse, two call sites can observe different settings if .env changes mid-run. lru_cache is safe because tests construct Settings() directly or patch module globals.

nodes.label: F14: SSE Translator Duck-Types the Retrieve Step
nodes.rationale: Matching 'the retrieve step' by checking whether the output dict contains retrieved_docs breaks silently if any future chain step carries that key, and the == [] sentinel cannot distinguish 'retriever returned nothing' from 'not seen yet'. Fix names the step via with_config(run_name='retrieve') and uses an explicit seen flag.

nodes.label: F15: No Timeout Around the LLM Stream
nodes.rationale: A hung upstream call keeps the SSE connection, generator, and resources open indefinitely — slow-drip resource exhaustion during upstream incidents. Fixed with asyncio.timeout (Python 3.11) reusing F4's error-then-done path.

nodes.label: F16: Missing SSE Anti-Buffering Headers; /health Lies Before Init
nodes.rationale: Without Cache-Control: no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no, nginx buffers the stream and silently destroys the token-by-token UX. Separately, initialize_app_state happily builds a chain with an empty API key so a misconfigured deploy passes health checks and fails every request — hence a separate /ready readiness probe and a startup ValueError.

nodes.label: F17: Classifier Output Unguarded Against Shape and Logit Surprises
nodes.rationale: A different head width raises IndexError deep in the request and a logits head yields confidence > 1.0 which fails DetectionResult's le=1.0 as an opaque 500. Model swaps are expected here. Also flags for human verification that EfficientNetB3's canonical input is 300x300 while the code says 224 — explicitly do NOT change it without confirming against the trained artifact.

nodes.label: F18: Safety Keyword Checks Use Bare Substring Matching
nodes.rationale: 'film' matches 'biofilm' and 'stock' matches 'stockings', so legitimate skin queries get the canned off-topic refusal. False refusals on a medical education tool are a direct safety-quality regression, and this gate sits in front of every query. Word-boundary regexes still handle multi-word entries like 'tahi lalat' correctly.

nodes.label: F19: PubMed Parsing Truncates Abstracts and Mangles Dates
nodes.rationale: t.text returns only text before the first child element, and PubMed abstracts routinely contain <i>/<sup>/<b>, so abstracts are silently truncated on the way into the knowledge base — degrading the exact corpus the RAG system exists to ground on. Also PubDate/Month is a name ('Jan') so zfill is a no-op, and joining 500 PMIDs into one efetch GET URL breaks precisely at the advertised max_results.

nodes.label: F20: Log Rotation Not Multi-Worker Safe; All Paths CWD-Relative
nodes.rationale: The app only works when started from the repo root with a single worker: TimedRotatingFileHandler workers clobber each other's rotated files at midnight, and logs/templates/static/chroma/cache paths all resolve against CWD. Fix anchors everything to PROJECT_ROOT; for rotation, documenting the single-worker constraint is deemed acceptable rather than building a logging daemon.

nodes.label: F21: CLAUDE.md, architecture.md, README Describe a Codebase That No Longer Exists
nodes.rationale: All three claim RAG lives in utils/, that there is no server-rendered UI, and that the classifier returns a hardcoded mock — all false. These docs steer humans AND coding agents, so drift is actively harmful; the review itself had to rediscover the real structure by reading source. Scheduled last so docs describe the post-fix state.

nodes.label: F22: O(n^2) Response Accumulation in the Token Loop
nodes.rationale: full_response += token copies the whole string per token; accumulate into a list and join once.

nodes.label: F25: Dead Code (Unused Settings, Orphaned Accessor, Dead Template Context)
nodes.rationale: main.py's module-level settings forces a .env parse at import for no consumer; get_app_settings has zero callers; and chat_page builds session/label/confidence template context that chat.html never reads because the page pulls those from URL params in JS instead.

nodes.label: F27: Magic Numbers Scattered Across Modules
nodes.rationale: max_turns=6, temperature=0.3, 1500-char truncation, and batch_size=100 are hardcoded at call sites while sibling knobs like rag_top_k live in Settings. Defaults preserved exactly so no existing test changes behavior.

nodes.label: F30: Pydantic v1 Relics on the Retriever Adapter
nodes.rationale: Inner `class Config` is deprecated under Pydantic v2 and emits warnings; underscore attrs rely on private-attr inference plus a custom __init__. Also the adapter is misplaced in app_state and belongs beside EvidenceFilteredRetriever in retriever.py.

nodes.label: F33: log_query Records Identical Retrieved/After-Filter Counts
nodes.rationale: The route only ever sees post-filter output, so the pre-filter count the log schema implies is unknowable there. Two options offered — stash the pre-filter count in doc metadata, or accept equality with an explicit comment — but the log schema keys must not change because downstream eval reads them.

nodes.label: Severity Rubric (High/Medium/Low)
nodes.rationale: High = wastes money/tokens per request, blocks the event loop, leaks data, breaks the client contract, or violates a stated compliance guarantee. Medium = degrades contract/observability/robustness under realistic conditions. Low = mechanical cleanup.
